rows.basis: licensing page, section 'ADA Dental Terminology Licenses: Licensing for Commercial Users'
rows.quote: Except as permitted by law, all use, copying or distribution of CDT, or any portion thereof (including the Code on Dental Procedures and Nomenclature) in any product or services (including works prepared for clients by consultants and other professionals), whether in printed, electronic or other format, requires a valid commercial user license from the ADA.
rows.section: ADA Dental Terminology Licenses: Licensing for Commercial Users
rows.notes: Same sentence appears verbatim in the sell sheet PDF. The only carve-out language is 'Except as permitted by law' — the page does not define it.

rows.quote: With commercial use, you must bundle the Codes with other assets in your product or service and redistribution of the CDT Codes alone is not permitted.
rows.notes: Governs redistribution of the code set in software: codes may only be distributed bundled with other assets, never alone.

rows.quote: Because there are a number of ways to bundle the CDT Codes with your product or service, the ADA has a number of different license types including, but not limited to: software, published materials (print or digital), seminars/webinars, consultants, benefit plans or TPAs.
rows.notes: 'software' is an explicitly named licence type.

rows.basis: licensing page and sell sheet, searched for 'fair use', 'non-commercial', 'noncommercial', 'free of charge', 'no charge', 'royalty-free', 'identification', 'educational'
rows.notes: No free, non-commercial, educational, 'fair use' or 'identification-only' exemption statement exists on the licensing page or in the sell sheet (both searched; fetch result for the page: 'No such sentence appears on this page.' and 'None found on this page.'; sell sheet: 'Not addressed'). The only qualifying phrase is 'Except as permitted by law'. Do not infer an exemption.

rows.basis: ADA News article 'CDT is ADA intellectual property, source of revenue for association', May 25, 2023, by David Burger
rows.quote: Licensees pay annual royalties for their usage of CDT within their products and services. These commercial users of CDT include third-party payers, publishers and practice management software vendors.
rows.notes: Secondary (ADA's own news outlet, not the licence terms). Same article: 'The Association audits licensees' annual CDT usage reporting to ensure accuracy.'

rows.quote: Dentists, dental teams and hospitals do not need a license to use CDT. When dentists purchase a copy of the CDT manual, it includes the right to use the code in a practice and use CDT within practice management software.
rows.notes: This is the only 'does not need a license' statement found, and it concerns dentists/dental teams/hospitals purchasing the manual — not software developers, websites, consumers or non-commercial projects.
